relevance_note: The paper reports a Japanese family in which six patients with Behçet's disease over four generations carried a heterozygous C243Y A20/TNFAIP3 variant ('for which all affected family members carried a heterozygous C243Y mutation in the ovarian tumour domain'), with individual-level clinical and genetic detail.
method_note: No script was used: every span was copied by hand from the Markdown file and checked against it by text search. Judgements. (1) The paper is a single-family case report, so study_type = 'case report' and cohort_size_as_stated = 6 (the authors' own 'six patients with BD ... over four generations'). (2) The family also includes a healthy younger brother who was tested and carries no TNFAIP3 variant; he gets an individuals row (relatives of an in-scope person are in scope) but no variants row, because the variants table is one row per (individual, variant); his negative result is recorded in his clinical_diagnosis_basis and here. (3) The variant is printed as 'C243Y' (protein form) and, with no c./p. prefix, as '728 G>A' and '(chr6_138197226_G>A, C243Y)'; I did not convert between notations, so variant_original_string = 'C243Y', genomic_coordinates_as_stated = 'chr6_138197226_G>A', and cdna_hgvs_as_stated / protein_hgvs_as_stated are null because no 'c.' or 'p.' string is printed. (4) Patient 6 was not available for sequencing ('Sequence analysis was not possible on patient 6'), so her variant fields (variant_type, zygosity, inheritance) are 'not reported' even though the abstract says all affected family members carried C243Y; her variant row keeps variant_original_string = 'not reported'. (5) The intron deletion ('three nucleotide deletions in an intron of upper exon 3') is mentioned only for patient 1 and has no printed description, so it got no variants row; the sentence that it was paternally derived was not used as parental_testing_statement because it concerns that deletion, not C243Y (no parental testing of C243Y is reported). (6) Variant-level statements (missense, heterozygous, 'suspected to be the gene responsible for autosomal-dominant BD') were applied to patients 1-5, who are shown to carry that same variant ('present in all familial patients with BD examined'); patient 6 and the healthy brother are excluded from them. (7) Contradiction: the abstract's 'all affected family members carried a heterozygous C243Y mutation' conflicts with the figure 1 legend that sequence analysis was not possible on patient 6. (8) Normal/negative findings recorded as excluded features: 'tests for autoantibodies ... were negative' (feature 'autoantibodies', patient 1) and 'None of the patients had exhibited ocular lesions of BD' (checklist item 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation', excluded for all six patients as 'inferred from group statement', because the sentence names the group and patient 6 is one of the six patients). (9) No table in this paper is a patient table, so no cell values were stacked and no source column exists; every source_reference_in_review is 'not reported'. (10) Ages given as '43-year-old', '17-year-old' etc. were treated as the age at the time of report (age_at_last_evaluation).
